knowledge:
- key_parameters: nModules=The number of modules/biclusters to extract (e.g., nModules=10) ;; margin=Specifies whether to calculate Jaccard Index or performance statistics on "row", "col", or "both" ;; best=Logical in JIdist; if FALSE, returns the full distance matrix instead of only the best matches ;; threshold=Threshold value used in binarize to convert continuous data to binary
- alternatives: Traditional clustering methods (Hierarchical clustering, k-means) or other biclustering methods (bimax, fabia, coalesce). iBBiG is preferred when analyzing sparse binary data with overlapping biclusters of varying sizes, aspect ratios, and high noise.
- when_to_use: When analyzing sparse binary (1,0) matrices, such as discretized p-values from meta-gene set enrichment analysis (meta-GSA) across hundreds of gene expression datasets, or any other binary genomic data where overlapping biclusters are expected.
- pitfalls: Applying iBBiG directly to continuous gene expression data without first binarizing or discretizing it, as the algorithm is strictly optimized for binary (1,0) matrices.

workflows.name: binary_biclustering
workflows.intent: Perform iterative binary bi-clustering on a binary matrix, visualize the resulting modules, extract sub-matrices, and save the results.
input: binMat@Seeddata (A binary matrix of 1s and 0s, representing associations such as discretized p-values)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the package and prepare the binary matrix ;; 2. Run the iBBiG algorithm to extract a specified number of modules ;; 3. Plot the biclustering results and generate diagnostic plots ;; 4. Extract the sub-matrices of the clusters ;; 5. Write the bicluster results to a text file
workflows.code:
library(iBBiG)
binMat<-makeArtificial()
res<- iBBiG(binMat@Seeddata, nModules=10)
plot(res)
drawHeatmap2(res@Seeddata, res, number=4)
biclustmember(res,res@Seeddata)
biclustbarchart(res@Seeddata, Bicres=res)
plotclust(res, res@Seeddata)
Modules<-bicluster(res@Seeddata, res, 1:3)
writeBiclusterResults("Modules.txt", res, bicName="Output from iBBiG with default parameters", geneNames=rownames(res@Seeddata), arrayNames=colnames(res@Seeddata))

workflows.name: expression_data_preprocessing
workflows.intent: Prepare continuous gene expression data for iBBiG analysis by binarizing or discretizing it.
input: BicatYeast (A continuous gene expression data matrix)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the continuous gene expression dataset ;; 2. Binarize the dataset using a specified threshold or discretize it into binary format

workflows.name: bicluster_comparison
workflows.intent: Compare iBBiG biclustering results against a gold standard or another clustering run using Jaccard Index distance and performance statistics.
input: binMat (An iBBiG gold standard or reference clustering object)
workflows.stages: 1. Calculate Jaccard Index distance between the clusters across rows, columns, or both ;; 2. Extract detailed performance statistics (accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV) comparing the results to the gold standard
workflows.code:
JIdist(res,binMat)
JIdist(res,binMat, margin="col", best=FALSE)
JIdist(res,binMat, margin="col")
JIdist(res,binMat, margin="row")
JIdist(res,binMat, margin="both")
analyzeClust(res,binMat)
analyzeClust(res,binMat, margin="col")
